body_text: PDF Version BEIJING, Oct. 31, 2025 (GLOBE NEWSWIRE) -- QuantaSing Group Limited (NASDAQ: QSG) (“QuantaSing” or the “Company”), a pop toy company dedicated to creating beloved collectibles and trend-defining experiences, today announced that it filed its annual report on Form 20-F for the fiscal year ended June 30, 2025, with the Securities and Exchange Commission on October 31, 2025. The annual report on Form 20-F can be accessed on the SEC's website at http://www.sec.gov and on the Company's investor relations website at https://ir.quantasing.com/financials-filings/sec-filings . The Company will provide a hard copy of its annual report containing the audited consolidated financial statements, free of charge, to its shareholders and ADS holders upon request. Requests should be directed to the Company’s Investor Relations Department at ir@quantasing.com . About the Company The Company, through its Here (奇梦岛) brand, creates collectible pop toys that spark joy and inspire global culture. With innovative design and storytelling at its core, the Company delivers immersive experiences that connect deeply with collectors worldwide. Guided by joy, integrity, wonder, and co-creation, the Company is building vibrant cultural ecosystems where fans shape and share dreams. For more information, please visit: https://ir.quantasing.com . title: Future-proofing transport in an era of accelerated change
summary: Explore how agile transport strategies and strategic partnerships can unlock resilience, flexibility and sustainability.
body_text: Perspective At a crossroads: future-proofing transport in an era of accelerated change Perspective At a Crossroads: Future-proofing Transport in an Era of Accelerated Change Introduction In today’s volatile landscape, businesses are facing a critical moment in transport strategy . With fleet renewal decisions looming, whether you purchase or lease, leaders are being asked to commit to solutions that may define their operations for the next five to ten years. But with rapid changes in technology, regulation and customer expectations, the risk of locking into long-term, costly and inflexible transportation models has never been higher. So how do you choose the right route forward? The answer lies in agility, enabled through strategic partnerships . What’s at stake: The hidden risks of going it alone Fleet decisions made today will define your operational agility tomorrow. But with the pace of change accelerating, businesses may not have the full picture to make the right choices alone, especially when it comes to vehicle type, fuel strategy or tech investment. Without the right insight, you risk investing in solutions that may not align with future needs. Internal teams often lack the bandwidth or expertise to manage compliance, optimization and innovation at scale. And external pressures are intensifying, including: Volatile fuel prices and inflation ESG reporting requirements and emissions targets Global supply chain disruptions, from port congestion and extreme weather to geopolitical instability and raw material shortages Rising consumer expectations for speed, visibility and flexibility, putting pressure on last-mile and delivery models “We’re at a true inflection point as the pace of change accelerates and today’s decisions will have an outsize impact on your future operations. Brands need guidance to navigate the road ahead with confidence.” Carl Hanson, Managing Director – Transport, GXO In short, the transport landscape is shifting, and businesses need to adapt with it. Why partnering with a specialist de-risks your strategy Outsourcing transport isn’t only about cost; it’s about building resilience in a fast-changing landscape. A specialist transport logistics partner brings deep expertise , scalable infrastructure and a consultative approach that helps businesses stay ahead of regulatory shifts, customer expectations and sustainability goals. Transport decisions made today will shape operations well into the 2030s, when many net-zero targets become binding. Without the right insight, businesses risk locking into fleet models that are costly to adapt, misaligned with future regulations or unable to meet evolving customer demands. A strategic partner helps mitigate these risks by offering flexible, future-ready solutions. Here’s what that looks like in practice: Regionally optimized, compliance-led transport solutions tailored to local regulations and market dynamics Carrier-neutral operations that reduce dependency and increase flexibility across geographies Shared fleets and collaborative backhaul strategies that cut emissions and costs by maximizing vehicle utilization Strategic access to alternative fuels and electric vehicle (EV) trials Technology-enabled planning and execution, from AI-powered route optimization to real-time tracking and automated freight audits Consultative sustainability planning, helping businesses align fleet strategy with long-term ESG goals A great partner’s approach should be tailored, not off-the-shelf. Whether you’re scaling across regions, navigating infrastructure constraints or rethinking fleet composition, the right logistics partner helps you make smarter decisions today , without compromising tomorrow. Across Europe and the U.S., GXO is supporting customers with customized solutions, from EV trials in urban centers to alternative fuel adoption in long-haul networks, ensuring sustainability progress is achievable wherever you operate. “Partnering with a specialist gives you control and clarity, offering a single source of truth across your operations. For example, our managed transport solution boosts efficiency and cuts costs, all while delivering the tailored support your business needs.” Willem Veekens, Managing Director, GXO Sustainability and tech: The backbone of smarter transport Technology and sustainability are now central to transport strategy, not just for efficiency, but for long-term viability. AI-powered route optimization, dynamic planning and real-time tracking help reduce mileage, fuel use and emissions. For example, GXO has helped customers remove hundreds of thousands of miles annually through smarter planning, cutting costs and carbon simultaneously. Meanwhile, alternative fuels like hydrotreated vegetable oil (HVO), liquified natural gas (LNG) and bio compressed natural gas (bioCNG), offer immediate emissions reductions where electric EVs aren’t yet viable. These aren’t just stopgaps; they’re strategic tools that help businesses decarbonize today while preparing for tomorrow. “The real value of partnership lies in seamless integration: technologies and fuel strategies tailored to your network, delivering measurable impact and supporting long-term sustainability goals.” Carl Hanson, Managing Director – Transport, GXO Real-world impact: B&Q’s low-carbon transformation GXO’s work with B&Q, a leading UK-based DIY and home improvement retailer, is a blueprint for a future-focused transport strategy. Together, we’ve developed and delivered a long-term glide path to net zero by 2040, transitioning the entire retail logistics fleet to alternative fuels and introducing electric vehicles across the network. Highlights include: 100% of the fleet now powered by LNG and HVO 17% mileage reduction through smarter planning and backhaul Launch of electric vans and HGVs, with more planned Shared infrastructure enabling other GXO customers to access LNG fueling to encourage greater adoption These initiatives reflect not just operational excellence, but strategic foresight. Don’t get stuck, get strategic Transport is no longer just a cost center; it’s a strategic lever. And in a world of ‘predictable unpredictability,’ agility is the new advantage. At GXO, we combine deep expertise, advanced tech and regional scale to help businesses stay flexible, compliant and competitive. Whether you’re rethinking fleet strategy or scaling across borders , the right partner makes all the difference.

title: Q4 2025 | Quarterly Newsletter
summary: Centralize lease data, collect utilization/attendance insights, track office-related invoices, and manage on-demand coworking programs. q4-2025-quarterly-newsletter
body_text: Happy Fall! The days are getting shorter and the weather is getting cooler. Read on below for product updates and resources to stay updated on the corporate real estate market. ‍ Cheers, Team FlexDesk ‍ Product Updates ‍ Portfolio Management Track lease information, anticipate rent escalations, and never miss a renewal date. ‍ ✨ Surface Area over Time: Admins now have the ability to store dynamic surface area figures over time for more precise reporting and calculations of derived metrics. ‍ 📝 Notes & Comments: Users now have the ability to collaborate within a lease record by adding notes, comments, and tagging others. ‍ ⚒️ UI enhancements: Admins have additional reporting capabilities, including breakouts by space type, rollups for an entire lease term, document library, and country-level rollups. ‍ Utilization Intelligence Leverage existing badge access systems to automatically track attendance, RTO compliance, and make smarter renewal decisions. ‍ 🔥 Department-level Analytics: Users now have filtering and grouping analytics by department. ‍ ⏳ Capacity/Headcount over Time: Users now have the ability to store dynamic capacity and headcount figures over time for more precise reporting and calculations of derived metrics. ‍ 💥 Dashboard enhancements: Users now have access to expanded reporting functionality, including quarterly breakouts, bulk-add annotations, and export functionality. ‍ Coworking Management Provide employees with drop-in access to thousands of coworking locations within one booking interface. Maintain spend controls and consolidated billing. ‍ 🚀 Cost Center allocation: Admins now have the ability to assign bookings to specific cost centers for invoice itemization. ‍ 🌐 Continuous Inventory Monitoring: High-traffic coworking brands now have daily monitoring jobs for continuous site and inventory refinements. ‍ 📱 Cancellation Policy: Users now have visibility into the coworking space’s cancellation policy at the time of booking. ‍ What We Are Reading And Writing A Workplace Experience Capability Crisis: Read Phil Kirshner’s blog post on the state of workplace capabilities, as surfaced from 50 different conversations with workplace leaders. Seasonality Matters in your CRE Data: Read David Music’s blog post on how seasonality impacts the assessment of workplace occupancy data. CRE/W Role Openings: The job market for corporate real estate & workplace continues to show promise.
